meta.purpose: Sourced firefighting resource data for CrisisTwin's fire-suppression simulation. Every leaf value carries source_id + page, or assumption=true + reason.
meta.units_note: Source units are kept (gallons, feet, chains, lb, knots); convert at the boundary: 1 chain = 20.1168 m, 1 ft = 0.3048 m, 1 gal = 3.78541 L, 1 kt = 1.852 km/h, 1 lb = 0.453592 kg. Percent grade = rise/run x 100.
meta.leaf_rule: A leaf is an object with a 'value' key. It must have 'unit' and either ('source_id' and 'page') or ('assumption': true and 'reason').
meta.fuel_models: Fire behavior fuel models are the 13 Anderson (1982) NFFL models used by the cited tables.

single_lane_speed_factor.reason: Narrow single-lane roads with oncoming traffic and blind curves slow heavy apparatus; no retrieved figure.

unpaved_speed_kmh.reason: No retrieved source; conservative planning speeds for heavy apparatus.

heavy_apparatus_speed_kmh_by_highway.reason: No retrieved source for emergency-driving speeds of heavy apparatus; ADR 0023 uses free-flow OSM speeds. These cap them. Calibrate with CAD AVL data when available. Applied as the level-road cap of the travel model (road_access.travel). Before 2026-10-24 the backend never applied it (it read speed_kph from road_access, which returns speed_kmh), so trucks drove at the OSM speed.

grade_speed_penalty.reason: Loaded engines slow on grades; no retrieved source. Superseded in backend drive times by the grade model of road_access.travel (level speed taken at grade 0); the Studio port still uses it.

nfpa1901_max_top_speed_mph.page: Highway Performance: max top speed GVWR over 26,000 lb 68 mph; tanks over 1,250 gal or GVWR over 50,000 lb 60 mph (NFPA 1901 as restated)

nfpa1901_acceleration.page: Highway Performance: 0 to 35 mph within 25 s on 0% grade (a minimum; used as the acceleration rate, conservative)

nfpa1901_min_grade_speed.page: Highway Performance: at least 20 mph on any grade up to 6% (check only)

rolling_resistance.page: Eq 4.7; Table 4.6 (asphalt good Cr 1.25); Table 4.7 (radial c2 0.0328, c3 4.575)

side_friction_by_design_speed_kmh.unit: f by design speed km/h (converted from mph)
side_friction_by_design_speed_kmh.page: Table 2B.1 (AASHTO 2018 Table 3-7), mph rows converted to km/h

superelevation.reason: Actual superelevation unknown. The Green Book allows 4-6% in urban areas and up to 8% as a reasonable maximum (CED C04-034 pp.7-8); 6% on highways (snow on the Paradise ridge) and 4% on local roads taken for every curve.

braking_decel_ms2.reason: The AASHTO stopping-sight-distance deceleration (3.4 m/s2), not retrieved in this change; used for braking into curves and junctions.

curve_min_half_chord_m.reason: Three-point circumradius uses neighbour vertices at least this far either side, so 1-2 m digitizing jitter on densely drawn OSM lines does not read as a tight curve. Not calibrated.

profile_step_m.reason: Sample spacing of the per-edge speed profile; the DEM is about 30 m, so finer adds no grade detail. Not calibrated.

junction_stop_dwell_s.reason: NFPA 1500 (2021, via VFIS p.2) requires a complete stop at stop signs and negative right-of-way intersections during emergency response; the time stopped is not sourced.

junction_caution_speed_kmh.reason: Speed an apparatus slows to where it meets a road of its own class (control unknown; due regard, CVC 21056). Not sourced.

rand_travel_time.page: T = 0.65 + 1.7 D (RAND, urban NYC; used by ISO); cross-check only

fixed_wing_retardant_window.value: Multi-engine airtankers are dispatched to arrive with no aerial supervision not earlier than 30 min after official sunrise and not later than 30 min before official sunset; retardant operations only in daylight; after official sunset only with flight-crew concurrence AND aerial supervision on scene. Daylight hours = 30 min before sunrise to 30 min after sunset. Empty multi-engine aircraft may fly to bases after daylight.
fixed_wing_retardant_window.page: PDF p.37 (printed p.41) 'Retardant Operations and Low Light Conditions'

airtanker_early_late_arrival.value: Airtankers may arrive as early as 30 min before official sunrise and may drop as late as 30 min after official sunset provided pilot judges visibility and safety suitable.

twin_engine_fixed_wing_night.value: Not limited to daylight if aircraft and pilot are IFR-equipped/authorised (agency policy applies).

helicopter_daylight_limit_min.page: PDF p.42; multi-engine helicopters not limited to daylight under certain stipulations (emergencies, lighted airports)

usfs_night_helicopter.value: USFS low-level night helicopter operations primarily use night-vision goggles; night operations VFR only, avoid fog and smoke, lights on.

calfire_night_helicopters.value: CAL FIRE S-70i Black Hawks are 'capable of nighttime aerial firefighting'.

visibility.value: Flights are suspended when poor visibility precludes safe operations, regardless of time of day.

smoke.value: Inversions hold smoke in valley bottoms, preventing visibility of the flight path; sun glare also limits visibility.

wind_retardant_ineffective_mph.page: p.172 'Retardant generally is ineffective when wind speeds exceed 20 mph' (1996; older, lower than IASG 2017)

hard_flight_wind_limit_kt.reason: Neither IASG nor PMS 465 gives a fixed maximum flight wind; they say operations stop at pilot discretion for safety of flight. 35 kt sustained is an assumed hard stop for the model.

density_altitude_ft.page: p.167: performance usually begins to be affected above 4,000 ft density altitude

dip_or_reload_distance.reason: No retrieved limit; chosen so that helicopter cycle stays near the sourced 3-5 min turnaround and airtanker cycle near the sourced one-hour cycle at 230-300 kt cruise.

flame_length_limit_ft.page: p.171, 174: retardant inappropriate for direct attack above 8 ft flames

calfire_engines_web.page: fire.ca.gov mobile-equipment page via search summary (unverified)

calfire_dozers_web.page: fire.ca.gov mobile-equipment page via search summary (unverified)

calfire_initial_attack_goal.value: Contain 95 percent of all fires at 10 acres or less.

calfire_initial_aircraft_response.page: 'generally consisting of an Air Attack, two Air Tankers, and a Helicopter'; may be augmented by fire weather and history

initial_attack_ground_first_alarm_sra_hi.reason: No public CAL FIRE unit preplan or ECC dispatch matrix was retrieved (they are not published; contract-county and unit plans differ). Shape follows the SRA response described by the calfirepilots page (engines, dozers, crews, chiefs, air); counts are a placeholder for the simulator.

move_up_and_cover.value: Neighbouring-station engines relocate to the emptied station when the nearest unit commits; typical trigger: nearest station out for >30 min
move_up_and_cover.reason: Concept is standard practice but no CAL FIRE document with thresholds was retrieved.

strike_team_composition.reason: Common NWCG definition; not re-fetched here.

engines_per_station_estimate.reason: Derived: 343 year-round engines (house testimony p.3) / 220 active state-owned stations of type FSA/FSB/FSAB in tools/ca_fire_bases.json (196 FSB + 22 FSAB + 2 FSA). Seasonal and local engines excluded; single-engine stations are common, so this is an average.

turnout_s.page: 4.1.2.1 (fire turnout 80 s); as used in ADR 0023; NOT re-verified

travel_first_engine_s.page: 4.1.2.1 (first engine company, 90th percentile, urban career); NOT re-verified; rural SRA is much longer

wildland_turnout_s.reason: Volunteer and call-back stations and wildland engines on duty typically exceed the NFPA 1710 80 s; no retrieved figure. Use 80 s for staffed CAL FIRE stations, 120+ s otherwise.

helicopter_call_to_takeoff_min.reason: No retrieved figure for CAL FIRE helitack (crew assembles, hook-up, start). Aviation contract reaction time for helicopters is not in the retrieved documents.

hand_crew_mobilization_min.reason: Crews are housed at conservation camps or crew bases, not stations (ADR 0023 notes this); crew turnout from camp assumed 30 min. No retrieved figure.

dozer_mobilization_min.reason: Dozers need a transport rig and lowboy driver; no retrieved figure.

water_tender_refill_min.page: Water Tenders > Water Tender Typing Standard table (Max refill time row, Support types)
